longest_story.title: The Mystery Gadget from the Stars!
longest_story.first_line: No matter how dangerous for us, we must...
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Ed Manos (herb collector); Mr. French (store owner); Benny; the Harris Boys (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: A weird alien device is discovered, whose rays causes objects to evolve. The Caped Crusaders must battle a criminal gang into whose hands the device has fallen.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The False Face Society
longest_story.first_line: In Gotham City, a series of strange crimes begins with...
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Mr. Van Brunt (wealthy man); The Joker (villain); The False Face Society (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman goes undercover as a member of the False Face Society in order to get the goods on and capture the leader.
longest_story.notes:
Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

Anthony Durrant hypothesizes, "It seems to me that running the False Face Society is not the Joker's cup of tea, as none of the crimes in this story would appear to have a prankish twist; in fact, they are very different from his original method of operation. Perhaps he was not originally intended to be the secret leader of the False Face Society, as he only appears unmasked at the very end of this story."

longest_story.title: Chapter 3: Dimension of Doom
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Batwoman [Kathy Kane]; Bat-Girl [Betty Kane]; several alien troops; Karn (villain); Zebo (villain)

longest_story.title: Danger Strikes Four
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne] (mainstream); Batman II [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennyworth (mainstream); Robin [Dick Grayson] (mainstream); Robin II; Bruce Wayne; Bruce Wayne Jr.; Kathy Kane Wayne; Hal Durgin (villain); "Stogie" Rand (villain, Durgin's henchman); Durgin's unnamed henchman (villain); Magog (villain, robot); Big Al Finney (villain); Big Al's gang (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: As Dick begins reading Alfred's latest imaginary tale of Batman II and Robin II, he is called upon by the Caped Crusader to battle Big Al and his men, with all involved in circumstances strangely resembling Alfred's story.
longest_story.notes:
Script credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

This is the fourth in a series of imaginary tales of Batman II and Robin II written by Alfred.  Last seen in the third story of Batman #145 (February 1962), next in the second story of Batman #159 (November 1963).  The events in Alfred’s story are not part of regular continuity.
longest_story.keywords: Alfred's Tales of the Future; Gotham City; Imaginary Story; Wayne Mansion

longest_story.title: Batman's Psychic Twin
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Kathy Kane; Jo-Jo Gagan (villain, death); Boss Bragg (villain, crime boss); Bragg's gang [Luke; Tobin; others unnamed] (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: A rare chemical explosion psychically links Batman with Jo-Jo Gagan, and when the underworld finds out about this, they turn on Gagan and attempt to kill him, believing that the Caped Crusader will perish as well.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Robin Dies at Dawn, Chapter 1
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennyworth; Ace the Bat-Hound; Commissioner James Gordon; unnamed Army doctor; Gorilla Gang [Pete; Luke; one unnamed] (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman undergoes a test simulation for a situation that astronauts may one day face alone in outer space, and during that simulation he sees Robin die. After the test is over, Batman faces the terrible side-effects of his simulation, believing that Robin will actually die, and it so complicates his fight against crime, he decides to retire!
longest_story.notes: Story told in two chapters.
longest_story.keywords: Bat-Cave; Bat-Signal; Batmobile; Gotham City; Wayne Mansion

longest_story.title: The Hunt for Batman's Secret Identity

longest_story.synopsis: When Mirror Man escapes from prison and reforms his gang, he once again tries to prove his belief that Batman is Bruce Wayne...and he does...and doesn't!
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Ace -- the Super Bat-Hound

longest_story.synopsis: Bat-Mite shows up again to have some fun and decides to give Ace some super powers, which he uses to aid the Caped Crusaders. However, when Ace chases crooks into a cave, the mine fumes cause havoc with the dog's super powers, and he turns on the Dynamic Duo.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Great Clayface-Joker Feud
longest_story.characters: Bat-Girl [Betty Kane]; Batman [Bruce Wayne] (also as The Joker); Batwoman [Kathy Kane]; Clayface [Matt Hagen] (villain); Commissioner James Gordon; The Joker (villain); Robin [Dick Grayson]; Batman robot; three underworld hoods (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: After escaping from prison, Matt Hagen finds a way to synthesize the liquid that turns him into Clayface, and once more takes up crime. The Joker, meanwhile, objects to Clayface getting all the headlines, so he starts a feud with Clayface.
longest_story.notes:
Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

Story in two chapters of 7.67 pages each.

longest_story.title: The Mystery of Madcap Island
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; the citizens of Madcap Island [Benson; others unnamed]; Bart (villain, a shopkeeper); Jason Reid (villain, leader of the Green Hood Gang); Ed Kiley (villain, Reid's henchman, death)
longest_story.synopsis: The Dynamic Duo track Ed Kiley to Madcap Island, home to numerous wealthy eccentrics, and discovers him murdered.
longest_story.notes: Script credit by Martin O'Hearn. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Bat-Mite Hero
longest_story.first_line: Hee-Hee! How do you like the way my new hero captured those crooks, Batman?
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Bat-Mite; Jerome Withers; The Blonde Bombshell; Bombshell's manager; Frank Collins (villain); Collin's gang (villains); Bill Strong (villain); Sexton Gang members (villains); The Human Fly bandits (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman corners a wanted felon in a baseball stadium, but Bat-Mite appears and messes things up with his magical nonsense. Batman tells him to find another hero to pester, so Bat-Mite creates a series of heroes (the third a crook), but they fail miserably.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Batman Creature!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Batwoman [Kathy Kane]; Bat-Hound [Ace]; Eric Barroc (villain, scientist, trained-beast creator); Barroc's henchmen (villains); the animal-men (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: A mad scientist has invented a ray which turns men into animal creatures, who steal for him. When he turns the ray on Batman, turning the Caped Crusader into a creature, it's all Robin, Batwoman and Bat-Hound can do to stop him.
longest_story.notes: Script credit from Martin O'Hearn at http://martinohearn.blogspot.com/. Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: The Joker Jury!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Commissioner James Gordon; The Joker (villain); Robin [Dick Grayson]; Joker's henchmen (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: The Joker begins a crime wave using the city's various departments as his theme. When the Caped Crusaders head out to battle the Crime Clown, they are captured and put on trial by the Joker.
longest_story.notes: Inker credit verified by Paris.

longest_story.title: Two-Way Gem Caper!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; The Hootenanny Hotshots (folk singers); Mr. Dabblo (villain); Dabblo's accomplice (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman discovers a plot to waylay a group of folk singers in order to perpetrate the theft of a pearl from a museum, and eventually nabs the villain after foiling a trap set for the criminal.
longest_story.notes:
Story in two parts of 7.67 and 5.67 pages.

Script credit from Batman (DC, 1940 series) #167. Editor Julius Schwartz's pay records have Bob Kane on pencils. However, it is known that Bob Kane contracted the artwork out to Sheldon Moldoff.

This story introduces several new elements to the "New Look" Batman. Batman has redesigned the Bat-Cave with an automatic elevator leading to Wayne Manor. The Batmobile has also been redesigned into a sports car. The Bat-Cave exit is no longer a barn, it is now a hidden door on a hillside and leads to the highway.
 
Batman also uses a Hot-Line phone which links the Batmobile (later on the Bat-Cave, too) to Commissioner Gordon's office. Gordon's physical appearance also looks younger and slimmer than prior appearances.
longest_story.keywords: Bat-Cave; Batmobile; Gotham City; Hot-Line; Wayne Mansion

Detective Mike Powell [Bulldog] (Patricia's father, introduction); Professor Ralph Smedley (chemist, introduction); gang of hi-jackers (villains); two kidnappers (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: Patricia Powell graduates from the Police Academy with top honors and receives her rewards from the Batman, whom she tells that she has a great affection for Bruce Wayne.

Script credit from Batman (DC, 1940 series) #167. Editor Julius Schwartz's pay records have Bob Kane on pencils. However, it is known that Bob Kane contracted the artwork out to Sheldon Moldoff.

This story continues in part in the second story of Batman #166.

longest_story.title: A Rendezvous with Robbery!

longest_story.synopsis: Patricia Powell is hoping this is the time she finally meets Bruce Wayne, but things go awry when someone robs the Wayne Estate.
longest_story.notes:
Editor Julius Schwartz's pay records have Bob Kane on pencils. However, it is known that Bob Kane contracted the artwork out to Sheldon Moldoff.

This story is continued in part from the second story of Batman #165. 

A caption at the end of the story indicates that a follow-up to this story was planned, but was never published.

longest_story.notes: The writer credit is found in Batman #169.

The script credit is found in Batman #169. Credits for script and inks confirmed from Julius Schwartz's editorial records, provided by DC Comics. Records show that Bob Kane was paid for the pencils, but scholars agree that pencils were actually by Moldoff.

Story in two parts of 5.67 and 6.67 pages.

longest_story.title: Remarkable Ruse of the Riddler!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Smiles Dawson (introduction); Roger Peale (introduction); The Riddler [Edward Nigma] (villain, has 5-page history); Riddler's gang (villains); Molehill Mob (villains)
longest_story.synopsis: The Riddler is released from prison and informs the Dynamic Duo that he has turned from crime, and, as proof, leads them to the hideout of the Molehill Mob. But when the former felon begins deluging them with riddles, the Caped Crusaders aren't sure he really has reformed.

Credits for script and inks confirmed from Julius Schwartz's editorial records, provided by DC Comics. Records show that Bob Kane was paid for the pencils, but scholars agree that pencils were actually by Moldoff.

Credits for script and inks confirmed from Julius Schwartz's editorial records, provided by DC Comics. Records show that Bob Kane was paid for the pencils, but scholars agree that pencils were actually by Moldoff.

Story in two parts of 5.67 and 6.67 pages.

longest_story.title: Secret Identities for Sale!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Commissioner James Gordon; Mayor of Gotham City; Johnny Jason (movie Star); Myra Holt (actress); Mr. Incognito [James Carter] (villain, introduction); Incognito's gang (villains, introduction for all); Elwood Pearson (villain, introduction)
longest_story.synopsis: While the Caped Crusaders are raiding the hideout of Mr. Incognito, a photographer takes pictures of the action with a special x-ray film, revealing the criminal's identity. longest_story.notes:
Credits for script and inks confirmed from Julius Schwartz's editorial records, provided by DC Comics. Records show that Bob Kane was paid for the pencils, but scholars agree that pencils were actually by Moldoff. 

Story in in two parts: unnumbered Part 1 (7.67 pages) and Part 2 (4.67 pages, title is same as for 1st part but without exclamation point).

longest_story.title: The Off-Again On-Again Lightbulbs!

longest_story.synopsis: When Batman arrives at the Wednesday meeting of the Mystery Analysts, a cleaning man enters and announces that it is actually Friday, and he can prove it with a copy of that day's paper. longest_story.notes:
Credits for script and inks confirmed from Julius Schwartz's editorial records, provided by DC Comics. Records show that Bob Kane was paid for the pencils, but scholars agree that pencils were actually by Moldoff.

longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; Alfred Pennyworth; Commissioner James Gordon; Mr. Rink (night watchman); unnamed prison warden; The Penguin [Oswald Cobblepot]; Lefty (villain); Duke (villain)

longest_story.title: The Loan Shark's Hidden Hoard!
longest_story.first_line: Batman is knocking out Mako! Now I'll have to settle with him myself – –!

longest_story.title: The Riddle-Less Robberies of the Riddler!
longest_story.first_line: I cued you no clues I was going to rob here, Batman and Robin...

longest_story.synopsis: After the Riddler breaks out of prison, he vows never again to send riddles to Batman before he strikes. The Caped Crusader smells a rat and discovers subtle clues that lead to the Riddler's downfall.

longest_story.title: Death Knocks Three Times!
longest_story.first_line: Sooner or later, every criminal, no matter how powerful, how clever, has been brought to justice by Batman and Robin!
longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; a Yogi (introduction); Death-Man (villain, introduction, death); Death-Man's gang (villains, introduction for all)
longest_story.synopsis: Batman stops a crook in a skeleton costume who boasts that he will escape justice. On the way from the courtroom, the man falls over and apparently dies, a fact that haunts the Batman, especially when he thinks of the man's boast. When Death-Man reappears, the Caped Crusaders get him again, only to have him die a second time, only to be resurrected again. Batman wonders: will the third time be the "lucky" charm that ends this menace?
longest_story.notes:
Credits for script and inks confirmed from Julius Schwartz's editorial records, provided by DC Comics. Records show that Bob Kane was paid for the pencils, but scholars agree that pencils were actually by Moldoff.

Story across 24 pages in three parts of 5.67, 5.67, and 11.67 pages.

longest_story.title: The Perfect Crime -- Slightly Imperfect!

longest_story.characters: Batman [Bruce Wayne]; Robin [Dick Grayson]; a Batman impostor (villain); impostor's gang (villains)

longest_story.synopsis: While investigating criminal activity at a transport company, Batman recognizes the owner, Joe Chill, as the man who killed Thomas and Martha Wayne years before.
